findings.detail: If git emits the main worktree record and then fails or is interrupted before listing another live worktree, live_worktrees_json accepts the truncated inventory as complete. decorate_claims marks the omitted holder stale, so check reports its resource free, claim can replace it without takeover approval, and prune can delete it. This defect predates the range; the added exception explicitly leaves it deferred.
findings.evidence: At line 230, process substitution discards the inventory producer's status. Any emitted field sets saw_any=1, and the final jq can return success. Lines 507-524 consequently set live_known=yes and mark omitted holders stale. Lines 826-851 allow replacement of stale claims; lines 954-963 remove them during prune. The base commit contains the same implementation. In contrast, launch-workmux:137 checks the captured inventory command's status.
findings.title: Absent or partial data: failed worktree inventory can release live resource claims

findings.detail: The single-issue validator accepts concatenated JSON objects. Input containing {"number":1,"title":"One","state":"OPEN"} followed by {"number":2,"title":"Two","state":"OPEN"} passes validation and produces a malformed single-issue prompt with combined numbers and titles, while returning success. This defect predates the range.
findings.evidence: jq empty accepts a JSON stream, and jq -e 'type == "object"' succeeds for both objects. Each jq_value extraction processes both documents, making number equal to "1\n2" and title equal to "One\nTwo" before the single prompt printf at line 144. The sibling read_claims validator at lines 291-299 explicitly counts documents and rejects multiple values. The base commit has the same issue-validation and extraction logic.
findings.title: Validator gaps: concatenated issue objects pass the single-object validation
